---
title: "Hardware Overview"
---

## Bill of materials

| Component | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| Arm | Braccio V2, 6-DOF: base, shoulder, elbow, wrist-vertical, wrist-rotation, gripper |
| Arm controller | Arduino Mega running stock Braccio firmware at `/dev/ttyACM0` |
| Sensor controller | Teensy 4.1 at `/dev/ttyACM1` |
| ToF | 4 x VL53L5CX on a TCA9548A I2C mux, 8x8 distance grid per sensor |
| IR | 4 x EC-Buying IR obstacle sensors, active-LOW at 5 V, through a TI SN74LVC02A NOR-inverter stage to 3.3 V active-HIGH on Teensy pins 23, 22, 21, 20 |
| IMU | MPU-6050 on the Teensy, accelerometer-derived roll and pitch |

## Serial wiring

The two microcontrollers each present a USB-CDC endpoint. The controller opens both at 115200 baud:

```
Host ── USB ──> Arduino Mega (/dev/ttyACM0)  ── PWM ──> Braccio servos
Host ── USB ──> Teensy 4.1    (/dev/ttyACM1) ── I2C ──> TCA9548A mux ── 4x VL53L5CX
                                              ── GPIO ──> 4x IR via NOR inverter
                                              ── I2C ──> MPU-6050
```

## Coordinate frame

The world frame sits at the arm base and shoulder pivot:

- `+X` points forward at theta 0°.
- `+Y` points left at theta 90°.
- `+Z` points upward.
- `theta` is the base rotation angle in degrees, 0 to 180.
- `r` is the radial reach in millimetres.
- `z` is the height above the shoulder pivot in millimetres.

The safety stack, the IK solver, and the UDP telemetry packets share this frame, so any sensor reading posted in world-frame coordinates plugs straight into the collision checker.
